anchors.static_observation: Claim creation uses onlyProtectedWallet and onlyMatchingPolicy; source caller identity is protected wallet, not necessarily policy holder.

This function is onlyOwner. It accepts owner-supplied historical wallet balance and a block number matching the configured depeg block. It does not verify a historical account proof or real-world truth.
A malformed individual wallet/block entry is skipped and emits an error event, while valid entries can be stored. This is not a whole-batch executor refusal.
Owner can overwrite a stored balance at this point; a frozen/final attestation assumption is not automatically enforced by this assignment.
Claim creation requires depegged product state, policy unexpired at depeg, within grace, and no prior claim, via policyIsAllowedToClaim; failure reverts DP-030.
Creation records a claim and expires the policy, then queues processing. Claim creation/expiry is not payment or disappearance of the obligation.
Processing is public and state-gated, not onlyOwner; authority enters through claim creation, owner balance entry and underlying GIF services.
An unqueued/already-removed processId is rejected before processing. Formal at-most-once success requires transaction/call-path assumptions and source state semantics.
A queued claim with no stored depeg block for its protected wallet reverts. This is a concrete missing-attestation refusal candidate.
A zero attested balance is a separate explicit refusal; it is not successful zero payout.

Across-policy processed balance is subtracted from attested wallet balance, then caps protected amount. If owner later lowers balance below processed balance, Solidity checked subtraction can revert before the explicit exhausted-balance guard.
Processing consumes protected token amount across policies, distinct from payout-currency amount. Operation order matters when coverage is oversubscribed.

The path confirms claim, creates payout, calls GIF payout processing, and closes policy; actual GIF service/controller/treasury semantics and custody are required to establish discharge, not merely these call names.
Claim formula uses integer truncation and a source-defined protected minimum depeg price. Preserve token units, price scale, coverage cap, arithmetic bounds and remaining residue.
Owner sets a historical block number after recorded depeg. The require only establishes depeg state; supplied block correctness is an external data assumption.
Test data setter is onlyOwner and onlyTestnet. Mainnet/goerli branch forwards configured aggregator data; local injected observations are not live feed execution.

scope: Static source navigation. No compiler, contract execution, Lean proof, deployed identity or source-entry acceptance.
